waiting.title: 42043 Mercedes-Benz Arocs 3245, function 11: the wheels move and the differential's case stays
waiting.what: A change to a function list. Function 11 (the rear axles’ differentials) holds the drive shaft still and turns one wheel of the third axle; its note says the other wheel then turns the opposite way. But the list names the differential’s case (p2036) as the part that moves. With the drive shaft held the case cannot turn: the shaft holds it. The change names the two wheels (p2219, p2227) as the parts that move and the case as the part that stays.
waiting.effect: Function 11 goes from partly working to working. The worker checked this on its branch with the whole set; preview keeps the old list and the old result until you sign.
waiting.confidence: High: it is what a differential does with its drive held, and what the function’s own note says. The worker tried it in the viewer (the model lifted, the drive shaft’s universal joint p2029 frozen, the collision pass ready): a turn of one wheel by half a radian turns the other by half a radian the opposite way, and the case stays still.

waiting.title: 9397 Logging Truck: the published file is the set's second model, the snowplough
waiting.what: The OMR has one file for this set, and it is the alternate model (the OMR page names it “Snowplow”): a truck with a yellow blade in front, no crane and no outrigger legs. Our function list was written from the booklets, which build the logging truck with its crane. So functions 2 to 6 (outriggers, crane slewing, boom, jib, log grab) name parts the file does not have. Functions 1, 7, 8 and 9 (motor and gearbox, steering, engine, wheels) hold for both models. Claude’s decision: the list is rewritten for the snowplough, because the goal is the models the OMR publishes. The worker finds LEGO’s instructions for the second model and drafts the list; the new list then comes to you to sign. Tell Claude if you want something else, for example to leave the crane’s functions as “not in the file”.
waiting.effect: Today the set counts 5 functions as working, 3 as partly working and 1 as not checked. Function 5 (the jib) counts as working although the file has no jib, so that count is not to be trusted until the list is rewritten. No correction to the file can mend this.
waiting.confidence: High that the file is the second model: the OMR’s own page for the set lists only “Snowplow”, the file’s one model is named 9397B, and the booklet’s outrigger legs (book 3, page 7) are not in it.
